subject: Re: Acme - pricing estimate & cost model
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Jill Park <jill.park@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Acme: call recap + next steps (cost model attached)

Jill — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from today's discovery: 

- Confirmed primary use case: customer support summarization + contextual QA for knowledge base (avg prompt length ~750 tokens, avg response ~1,200 tokens).
- Expected concurrency: ~25 concurrent users at peak; expected monthly active users ~5,000.
- Rough monthly token estimate (we discussed): 250M
1.2B input+output tokens depending on cadence.
- Customer goals: stay under ~$1,000
$2,500 / 1M tokens (targeting $/1M token unit economics). Budget band you mentioned: $60k
$250k annually.

I've attached a first-pass cost model and a simplified pricing calculator that maps model choice, quantization, and batching to monthly cost and per-1M-token unit price. High-level notes in the spreadsheet include recommended model variants and where batching/prefix caching saves the most.

Attachments: Acme_Redwood_Cost_Model_v2.xlsx (cost model), Redwood_pricing_calculator.csv (calculator)

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm the expected monthly active users and average calls per user (or share any telemetry)? That will tighten the token range.
2) Any procurement constraints (PO process, required billing terms, or SSO/KMS needs)?
3) I'll follow up with a one-page invoice estimate and a few pricing scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive) by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Thanks Sean — appreciate the recap and the quick turnaround on the model. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The 250M
1.2B token range sounds right as a starting estimate. Our engineering telemetry suggests 600M tokens/month for the initial rollout (conservative), with a potential to scale to ~1B within 6
9 months.
- For procurement: we need a standard SOW and a net-45 payment term. We also require data residency notes; Acme needs SOC 2 + confirmation that logs can be retained for 12 months and exported on request.
- Can you provide a target invoice that shows unit costs for three scenarios (600M, 1B, 1.2B tokens) and a blended $/1M token value? Also please include the assumptions about model used (e.g., open-variant-1.3B quantized), batching efficiency, and KV cache hit rate used in the calc.

Cc'ed procurement for visibility.

—Jill
Jill Park
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp
jill.park@acme.com

Subject: Re: Acme: pricing estimate & cost model (invoice scenarios attached)

Jill / team — thanks for the clarifications. Attached is a one-page invoice estimate (PDF) plus an updated cost model; I highlight the key assumptions below so procurement can review quickly.

Assumptions used across scenarios:
- Model: open-variant-1.3B quantized (Q4/8), on A100-class instances (Redwood Dedicated / hosted equivalent).
- Avg request: 750 tokens in, 1,200 tokens out = 1,950 tokens per exchange.
- KV cache hit rate: 18% effective token savings on average (prefix caching for common KB prompts).
- Batching / throughput optimizations: expected 12
18% additional token-efficiency at peak volumes.
- Discount tiers applied for committed monthly volumes (see spreadsheet rows).

Invoice scenarios (rounded):
- 600M tokens/month -> $64,800/month (~$108 / 1M tokens blended) -> $777,600 annual
- 1B tokens/month -> $99,500/month (~$99.5 / 1M tokens blended) -> $1,194,000 annual
- 1.2B tokens/month -> $115,000/month (~$95.8 / 1M tokens blended) -> $1,380,000 annual

I attached:
- Invoice_estimate_Acme_0319.pdf (one-pager with scenario totals and payment terms)
- Acme_Redwood_Cost_Model_v2.xlsx (updated: shows line-item unit costs, assumptions, and sensitivity knobs)
- Redwood_pricing_calculator.csv (calculator that outputs $/1M token given inputs)

Rishi — can you review the assumptions, particularly around the KV hit rate and batching efficiency? Monica — can you confirm the SLA and SOC2/data-retention language we should include in the SOW for procurement?

Next: once procurement confirms terms (net-45 ok?), I'll draft a short SOW and provide a DocuSign link for signature.
\Best,
Sean

Thanks team — quick notes from my side after reviewing the model: 

- KV hit rate 18% is reasonable given KB overlap; we'll mark a sensitivity row at 10%/25% so Acme can see upside/downside.
- Batching efficiency: we'll conservatively use 12% for the invoice; if they commit to a 12-month reserved capacity we can bake in 18% and a further discount tier.
- Procurement: net-45 is fine; we'll need to add standard SOC2 + data retention (12 months) verbiage in the SOW. Monica, please attach the SOC2 summary + sample SOW clause.

Sean — go ahead and send the DocuSign SOW once procurement confirms and I'll review the discount tier language before final.

-Rishi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
